newsitem.title: UK: Russia needs more effort to cut inflation - Dubinin.
newsitem.headline: Russia needs more effort to cut inflation - Dubinin.

text.p: Russia needs to step up efforts to bring inflation within its goal of one percent per month, but it will not rely on money supply limits alone, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Friday.

"In the first quarter of this year there has been little appreciation of the real exchange rate, so we need additional efforts to control inflation," he told a conference on Central and Eastern European capital markets.
Dubinin said annual inflation should be about 12 percent in 1997, down from about 22 percent last year when the increase in M2 money supply was about 34 percent.
"Last year the depreciation of the rouble against the dollar was less than inflation," he added.
He said monthly inflation in the first quarter of this year was averaging 1.5 percent, while depreciation of the exchange rate was less than one percent.
Dubinin told Reuters that intermediate money supply targets, which have been a key weapon in the fight against inflation in recent years, would continue to be used.
But he said a Lombard window had also been opened, allowing banks to borrow from the central bank using state securities, treasury bills and OFZ government bonds, as collateral.

"We have stopped strictly controlling part of the money supply by volume," he said. "We are counting more and more on automatic regulation, because this money is received by banks at a rather high interest rate."
Dubinin said this was a flexible market-based way of regulating the liquidity in the banking system and the economy as a whole.
"What is important is not so much quantitative limits to M2 or other money supply aggregates but strict observance of market demand for money," he said.
